# Playtest Bug Desk & Repro Triage Director: Getting Started

Turn playtest observations into reproducible issues, group duplicate reports and verify fixes against the affected build. This works for any genre: a bug is a bug whether it shows up in a puzzle board, a race, a story choice or a save file.

If `engine/lens.mjs`, `engine/lens-kit.mjs` or `fixtures/good-pack.json` are not on disk yet, write them byte for byte from the `bug-desk-triage-lens-engine` skill first (Node 18+, no dependencies).

## Words used here

- **Evidence pack:** one JSON file with the measurements for one build. The engine grades it.
- **Game profile (`pack.profile`):** the owner's settings, such as which bugs may be P0. Thresholds live here, never in the engine.
- **P0:** the top severity: stop and fix now.
- **Flaky:** a bug that happens on some runs and not others.
- **Case and receipt:** a case is one item the owner approved for checking (for example one high-priority ticket), listed in `profile.cases`. A receipt is the matching row under `receipts` that records what was run, on which build, and what happened.
- **gitSha and liveSha:** the source revision under review, and the build players actually run (the deployed or shipped build, or the build sent to testers).
- **U (UNMEASURED) and NOT_RUN:** U means no evidence yet and earns 0 points without counting as a defect. NOT_RUN means a test was planned but did not run.

## 1. Onboard one question at a time

Ask one question at a time, wait for the answer, then ask the next. Never stack questions in one message.

1. "Which game are we working on? Tell me its name, genre and the platforms it ships on." Then ask: "Which build should I look at first? A build id, commit or version number is enough." Then ask: "Where will the evidence come from: a CI run, a manual playtest capture or an export from your tracker?"
2. "Which kinds of bug count as P0 for your game, the ones where everyone stops and fixes them now? For example payments, lost or corrupted saves, or items players paid for. A single-player offline game might only use lost saves and crashes on start." Store the answer as `p0Scopes` in the profile.
3. "When a bug only happens some of the time, how many clean runs in a row should it pass before we call it fixed? The worked example uses 10 as a sample; choose what fits your game." Store the answer as `flakyRunsRequired`.
4. "Which issue tracker do you use? Can you give me a read-only export of open and recently closed tickets, with who fixed and who verified each one, plus severity, scope and confidence where you track them?"
5. "Does your game have share, invite or referral links that players send to each other? If not, I will leave that check out and it will show as not measured." Leave `shareIntake` out of the pack when the answer is no.
6. "Who should review my local ticket drafts before anything is filed?"

Before grading a real pack, check that its build and profile match what the owner chose. Record unavailable capture or execution as NOT_RUN. Use the populations (the sets of measured cases) listed by `node engine/lens.mjs --meta`.

## 2. What you provide

- An evidence pack (JSON) with `status: "VALID"`, a `liveSha`, a `gitSha` and a `packId` (all three are required), and an `artifacts` list. Every metric group names the artifact id it came from.
- Profile values in `pack.profile`: `p0Scopes`, `flakyRunsRequired` and the approved `cases`. A missing threshold makes its line U, never a default.
- Anything you cannot capture yet stays out of the pack. It grades U (UNMEASURED), which is honest and costs no false defect.

Metric groups this engine reads, and the skill that fills each one:

| Group | Evidence type | What it holds | Skill |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repro` | trace | high-priority tickets and whether each replays | `minimal-repro-builder` |
| `flaky` | trace | flaky reports and runs done against the profile criterion | `minimal-repro-builder` |
| `captures` | trace | findings about play, and how many have a capture of the actual action | `minimal-repro-builder` |
| `liveBehind` | config | whether you checked if the live build is behind the source | `issue-draft-and-fix-verification` |
| `dedup` | trace | candidate duplicate pairs and what happened to each | `duplicate-report-grouping` |
| `severity` | static | severity, scope and confidence per ticket; P0 scopes used | `severity-and-regression-bisect` |
| `routing` | static | grading mistakes and how many went to the audit fix list | `severity-and-regression-bisect` |
| `closure` | trace | closed tickets with fixer, verifier and raw artifacts | `issue-draft-and-fix-verification` |
| `mismatch` | trace | closures allowed despite an artifact mismatch (must be 0) | `issue-draft-and-fix-verification` |
| `sla` | trace | age of the oldest open P0 (growth check only) | `severity-and-regression-bisect` |
| `crashIntake` | trace | crash reports with a build id, triaged in the agreed window (growth check only) | `duplicate-report-grouping` |
| `shareIntake` | static | share or invite link reports (growth check only; leave out if your game has no such links) | `duplicate-report-grouping` |

## 3. Run the first grade

```
node engine/lens.mjs fixtures/good-pack.json   # worked example, synthetic, not a measurement
node engine/lens.mjs your-pack.json            # your build
node engine/lens.mjs --meta                    # rubric lines, weights and what each reads
node engine/lens.mjs --fixtures fixtures/good-pack.json  # negative and missing-input self-test
```

Read the record: `verdict` (PASS, CONDITIONAL, BLOCKED or INVALID), `grade` and `coverage`, then each line's `level` and `findings`, then `checks` (growth checks reported beside the grade, never scored) and `tickets` (candidate ticket drafts, already deduplicated).

## 4. Report in plain English

- Lead with the verdict, grade and coverage in one sentence. Say how much of the rubric was measured.
- List U lines as "not measured yet" with the capture that would measure them. Never call them defects.
- One local ticket draft per measured finding, with the pack id and artifact ids. Label any synthetic pack as synthetic.
- Rubric lines: reproducibility:1, reproducibility:2, evidence-completeness:1, evidence-completeness:2, correct-dedup:1, correct-dedup:2, severity:1, severity:2, closure-quality:1, closure-quality:2.
- Two rubric names need a plain reading. "Captures show real play" (`evidence-completeness:1`) means findings about play have a capture of real play, not only menus or loading; a "match" is any play session (a level, a race, a puzzle board, a story chapter). "Build lag recorded and applied" (`evidence-completeness:2`) means you recorded whether the build players run is older than the source, and capped scores read from its runtime logs when it is.

## 5. Skills in this template

- `duplicate-report-grouping`: Use when many crash reports, error logs, player reports or findings from other templates may describe the same bug: propose candidate duplicate groups for the human to confirm, and never merge different root causes automatically. Feeds `correct-dedup:1` and `correct-dedup:2`.
- `minimal-repro-builder`: Use when turning a crash, desync or player report into a replay that fails on the affected build, shrinking it to the smallest input that still fails, checking that captures show real play, and deciding when a flaky bug may leave flaky status. Feeds `reproducibility:1`, `reproducibility:2` and `evidence-completeness:1`.
- `severity-and-regression-bisect`: Use when setting a bug's severity and confidence, keeping P0 to the scopes your profile allows, sending grading mistakes to the audit fix list instead of the bug list, and bisecting a working repro to the change that introduced the bug. Feeds `severity:1` and `severity:2`.
- `issue-draft-and-fix-verification`: Use when writing a reproducible bug report as a local draft for any tracker, recording which build players actually run, and checking that a fix was verified on the right build by someone other than the fixer before it closes. Feeds `closure-quality:1`, `closure-quality:2` and `evidence-completeness:2`.
- `bug-desk-triage-lens-engine`: the engine source and how to run it.

## Blockers to tell the owner about

- Needs your real ticket export; the worked example is synthetic.

Before capture, agree on the case ids and expected values in `profile.cases` (for example the high-priority tickets to replay and the closures to review). Run `node engine/lens.mjs --meta` for the required row fields and comparisons. Record one row per approved case under `receipts`, including its id, liveSha and artifact id. A skipped or stale case leaves its line U. The bundled rows and budgets are synthetic.

## Team inputs and outputs

This template works on its own. When other templates from the kit run in the same game project, they exchange files under `.grokbot-team/artifacts/<artifact>/` (read the newest file) and share an append-only memory under `.grokbot-team/memory/`. Team spec 1.0.0.

| `evidence-pack` (required, ^1.0.0) | the owner | the pack path the owner gives, or `.grokbot-team/artifacts/evidence-pack/` | Stop and ask the owner for a pack. Without one there is no grade; record NOT_RUN. |
| `tracker-export` (optional, ^1.0.0) | the owner | `.grokbot-team/artifacts/tracker-export/` | Continue: intake and closure receipts are NOT_RUN and their lines stay unmeasured; write "ASSUMPTION: no tracker-export available" in the report and ask the owner for a read-only export. |
| `ticket-draft` (optional, ^1.0.0) | 01 Game Feel, 03 Prop and Rig, 05 Game Loop, 06 Economy, 09 HUD, 10 Trailer, 11 Environment, 13 Audio, 14 NPC and Lore, 15 Server Fairness, 17 Sprites, 19 Store Page, 20 Patch Notes, 21 Access, 22 Live Service, 23 Support Desk, 24 Ledger, 25 Matchmaking, 26 Balance Patch, 27 Retention, 28 App Store, 00 Starter | `.grokbot-team/artifacts/ticket-draft/` | Continue: group only crash and player reports, and say cross-template grouping was not measured. |
| `incident-report` (optional, ^1.0.0) | 22 Live Service | `.grokbot-team/artifacts/incident-report/` | Continue without it. Start the report with "ASSUMPTION: no support-case-draft available" and say which checks it would have informed. Leave lines that need it unmeasured. Never invent the missing data. |

After acting, save these outputs as local files for the human to review:

| Output | Format | Where | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ticket-draft` 1.0.0 | JSON or Markdown local draft | `.grokbot-team/artifacts/ticket-draft/` | 12 Producer |
| `change-list` 1.0.0 | JSON (closures verified on the fixed build) | `.grokbot-team/artifacts/change-list/` | 06 Economy, 10 Trailer, 20 Patch Notes |
| `grade-record` 1.0.0 | JSON (the engine's grade record) | `.grokbot-team/artifacts/grade-record/` | 12 Producer |

Each output file is JSON with `artifact`, `version`, `producer` (this template's id and version), `createdAt` (UTC), `synthetic` and `items`, as the kit's `spec/artifacts/<artifact>.schema.json` describes. Name files `<UTC date>-<short label>.json` so the newest sorts last.

Shared memory:

- Before acting, read `decisions`, `incidents`, `releases` from `.grokbot-team/memory/<topic>.jsonl`. Skip records that have expired or that a later record supersedes.
- Write only `decisions`, `releases`. Append one line per record with `engine/team-memory.mjs` (or the same JSON by hand): id, UTC time, writer (`gbf-18-bug-desk-triage` and `1.0.1`), topic, kind, summary, data, source, confidence (measured, reported or assumed), expires_at and supersedes. Never edit or delete a line; supersede it.
- Never put secrets, names, handles, wallets, emails or raw user ids in memory. Refer to a person or account only by `node engine/team-memory.mjs hash <id>`, which needs the salt in `GROKBOT_TEAM_SALT`. Run `node engine/team-memory.mjs lint` before you finish.
- Keep `.grokbot-team/` out of a public game repository (add it to `.gitignore`); in a private one, commit it so the append-only rule can be checked against history.

# Group duplicate reports

Many reports can describe one bug, and one vague report can hide two bugs. This skill proposes groups. Only the human merges, after reviewing a local candidate draft.

Rubric lines this feeds: `correct-dedup:1` and `correct-dedup:2`. Growth checks (reported beside the grade, never scored): `crash-intake`, and `share-link-intake` only if your game has share, invite or referral links.

## Words used here

- **Dedup key:** what makes two reports the same bug: root cause area, reproduction signature and build id.
- **Reproduction signature:** a short label for how the bug shows up when replayed, for example `save-in-shop > empty-inventory-slot`.
- **Candidate pair:** two reports that a similarity measure says might be the same bug. A candidate is a suggestion, never a merge.
- **Other templates:** every template in the kit (HUD, Audio, Access and so on) drafts its own findings. The same bug can arrive from several of them.

## Method

1. Normalize each report. For crash reports and error logs: strip memory addresses, line numbers that shift between builds, player ids and timestamps; keep the top stack frames and the error type. For player reports and findings from other templates: keep the build, the screen or level, the player's action and the visible symptom.
2. Propose candidates. Compare the normalized reports with any similarity method (splitting the text into short overlapping chunks and comparing them with MinHash is one common choice; plain text distance works for a small queue). Tune the cutoff on past reports you have already labelled. The cutoff only proposes pairs.
3. Review. Draft the evidence for each candidate pair locally: both signatures, both builds, and a replay of each when one exists. Count the pairs that are really different bugs (`dedup.distinctPairs`) and how many of them stayed separate (`dedup.distinctPairsKeptSeparate`). Count the confirmed same-root pairs (`dedup.sameRoot`) and how many the human merged (`dedup.sameRootMerged`). Record every candidate pair in `dedup.pairs` with `sameRoot` and `autoMerged`. Any pair merged by a script without a human counts against the line.
4. Crash intake. Every crash report carries the build id it came from and is triaged inside the window your team agreed: `crashIntake.received`, `crashIntake.withBuildSha`, `crashIntake.triagedInWindow`.
5. Share, invite and referral links (only if your game has them). A report about a broken link carries a sample of the failing link and reaches the person who owns those links, often whoever runs marketing or growth: `shareIntake.reports`, `shareIntake.withLinkSample`, `shareIntake.routedToLinkOwner`. If your game has no such links, leave `shareIntake` out of the pack. The check then reads U and never changes the grade.

## Examples (illustrative)

- 2D platformer: three players say "the jump is broken". Replays show two causes: a late jump just after leaving a ledge, and a collision seam on one tile. Two groups, not one.
- Farming or life sim: two crashes share the top frame in the save writer. One comes from saving in the shop, one from saving during a festival. Same frame, different callers: keep them separate until a replay shows one root cause.
- Turn-based strategy: the Audio and HUD templates both draft a finding about the same missing end-of-turn cue. One root cause from two templates: propose one merge for the human to confirm.
- Mobile puzzle: "board freezes" reports from two phone models with the same signature on the same build. A likely duplicate; confirm with one replay on each phone.

## Negative fixture

Feed two reports with near-identical stacks but different root causes; the gate must keep them apart. A good control pair: two failures with the same visible symptom and different replay signatures, one when loading a save and one when resuming from pause. They stay separate candidates until a human verifies a common root cause.

## Pitfalls

- Grouping by the top stack frame only, which merges unrelated crashes in shared helpers.
- Dropping the build id, so fixed and still-live crashes mix.
- Treating the similarity cutoff as a decision. It only makes a list for the human.

Gather evidence for: `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>` (see `bug-desk-triage-lens-engine`).

# Build a minimal repro

A repro (reproduction) is a recorded set of steps or inputs that makes the bug happen again on the same build. A minimal repro is the shortest one that still fails. A desync is when two copies of the game (two players, or a client and a server) disagree about the game state.

Rubric lines this feeds: `reproducibility:1`, `reproducibility:2` and `evidence-completeness:1`.

## Method

1. Record recent play. Keep a rolling buffer of the last stretch of play: the random seed, the player inputs and the key game state, plus server messages if the game has a server. Choose the length to suit the game's update or turn rate. Examples (illustrative): a racing game keeps the last few seconds of inputs at its fixed update rate; a turn-based strategy game keeps the last few turns and the seed; a narrative adventure keeps the choice log and the save slot; a mobile puzzle game keeps the board state and the tap sequence.
2. Save on failure. On a crash or desync, save the buffer with the build id. Agree on a time and attempt budget with the owner first. Record attempts, successful reproductions and elapsed time on the same build. If the replay could not run, record NOT_RUN.
3. Shrink. Remove half of the input stream and keep the cut if the bug still happens; repeat with smaller pieces (this is called delta debugging). Stop when removing any single step makes the bug go away.
4. Flaky bugs. A flaky bug happens on some runs and not others. It keeps flaky status until it passes the number of clean repeated runs set in your profile (`profile.flakyRunsRequired`). Record `flaky.flakyReports`, `flaky.criterionRuns` (the runs actually done) and `flaky.fixedBelowCriterion` (reports called fixed before the criterion was met; this must be 0).
5. High-priority reports. Every high-priority report needs a working replay: one row per ticket in `repro.highPriority` with `id` and `replayed`. Take the ticket list from a dated read-only export of your tracker. Record one row per approved case in `receipts.intakeReplay` with `ticket`, `signature`, `attempts`, `reproduced`, `rewind` (the trace artifact id of the replay) and `acceptance` (what a passing replay shows).
6. Captures of real play. A finding about play needs a capture of the play itself, not only a menu or a loading screen. The pack counts these as `captures.playFindings` (findings that claim something about a play session) and `captures.playFindingsWithActionCapture` (how many of them have a capture of the actual action). Here "match" means one play session of any kind: a level, a run, a race, a puzzle board, a story chapter or a round.

## Negative fixture

Remove the input that triggers the bug from a recorded repro and confirm the replay no longer reproduces it, so the check fails.

## Pitfalls

- A replay on a different build is not a repro. Record the build id.
- A capture of the title screen or a loading bar does not show the bug. Capture the action.
- Calling a flaky bug fixed after one clean run.

Gather evidence for: `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>` (see `bug-desk-triage-lens-engine`).

# Severity, confidence and regression bisect

Rubric lines this feeds: `severity:1` and `severity:2`. Growth check (reported beside the grade, never scored): `p0-response`.

## Words used here

- **Severity:** how bad the bug is for players. P0 is the top level: stop and fix now.
- **Confidence:** how sure the evidence is. A P0 with low confidence stays P0 and gets more evidence.
- **Audit defect:** a mistake in the review itself (a wrong rubric reading, a broken capture, a script error), not a bug in the game.
- **Regression:** something that used to work and broke in a later build.
- **Bisect:** test the builds or commits between the last good one and the first bad one, halving the range each time, until you find the change that introduced the bug.

## Method

1. Record severity and confidence as separate fields on every ticket: `severity.tickets`, each with `severity`, `scope` and `confidenceRecorded`. Never raise severity because confidence is high or because a report is loud.
2. Use P0 only in the scopes your profile allows (`profile.p0Scopes`). The pack lists the scopes actually used for P0 (`severity.p0ScopesUsed`). Examples (illustrative): an online game with purchases might allow `payments`, `entitlements` and `saved-state`; a single-player offline game might allow only `saved-state` and `crash-on-start`; a co-op game might add `session-join`.
3. Send audit defects to the audit fix list, not the game bug list. Count them (`routing.auditDefects`) and how many went to the audit list (`routing.routedToAuditList`). Draft each correction locally for human review.
4. Bisect. With a working repro from `minimal-repro-builder`, run it across the commits or builds between the last good and the first bad build. Use the time and run budget agreed with the owner. Skip commits that do not build or give an inconclusive result, and report the remaining range. Record the first verified bad commit and the files it touched in the local ticket draft.
5. P0 response time. Record the age in hours of the oldest open P0 in `sla.p0OpenHoursMax`, with a positive `sla.measuredCases`. If there is no open P0, leave `sla` out; the check reads U.

## Examples (illustrative)

- Racing game: one tester saw a replay ghost car drift off the track. Severity P2 (the race still finishes), confidence low (one sighting). Not P0, however sure the tester is.
- Narrative adventure: a choice is forgotten after loading a save. Scope `saved-state`, so P0 if the profile allows that scope; confidence rises to high once a replay fails every time.
- 3D arena game: a crash at round end that started recently. Bisecting between the last good build and the first bad one finds one commit that changed the scoreboard; three inconclusive builds are listed as inconclusive, not as good.

## Negative fixture

Mark a known good commit as bad in a test bisect and confirm the result is flagged as inconsistent. For the line itself: a pack that uses P0 for a scope that is not in `profile.p0Scopes` must drop `severity:1`.

## Pitfalls

- Bisecting a flaky bug with too few runs per step. Use the profile's run limits and mark inconclusive steps.
- Severity raised by how loud a report is rather than how many players it reaches.
- Filing a broken capture or a wrong rubric reading as a game bug.

Gather evidence for: `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>` (see `bug-desk-triage-lens-engine`).

---

description: "Use when writing a reproducible bug report as a local draft for any tracker, recording which build players actually run, and checking that a fix was verified on the right build by someone other than the fixer before it closes."
---

> **Audit contract v1 (overrides everything below).** Created by @meta_alchemist (https://x.com/meta_alchemist).
> - Score only with the rubric embedded in `engine/lens.mjs` (`LENS.rubric`, gbf-18-bug-desk-triage v1.3.0). `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>` computes the grade; this skill only gathers evidence for it and never adds points of its own.
> - Missing evidence is UNMEASURED (0 points, not a defect). A test that did not run is NOT_RUN, never PASS. Never invent a measurement; label every worked example synthetic.
> - Game facts and budgets come from your game profile (`pack.profile`). Treat sample numbers as illustrative. Set the frame-time budget separately for each target device in your game profile.
> - An automated gate needs a negative fixture that fails. Receipts carry measured values, never an unconditional PASS.
> Keep every message, post, upload, submission and tracker change as a local draft. Only the human reviews and sends, publishes, uploads or files it. Work only on a working branch. Push only when the human asks and only to that branch. Never push to main. The human merges and deploys. Any feature switch you add is off by default.

# Draft an issue and verify the fix

This works with any tracker: GitHub, GitLab, Jira, a spreadsheet or a plain text file. You write the draft locally. Only the human files it.

Rubric lines this feeds: `closure-quality:1`, `closure-quality:2` and `evidence-completeness:2`.

## 1. Draft the issue

Record the affected build, platform, settings, starting state and the expected player-facing outcome. Include a seed or save file only if it affects reproduction. Examples (illustrative):

- Mobile puzzle: the board state and the tap sequence.
- 2D platformer collision: the level file and the controller input trace.
- Turn-based strategy: the save from the turn before and the orders given.
- Farming or life sim: the save slot, the in-game day and the screen where it happened.

Replay on the affected build and record successes out of attempts. Remove unrelated steps while keeping the same visible failure (see `minimal-repro-builder`). Link the smallest cleaned capture, its build id, and the evidence that shows this is a new issue rather than an existing one (see `duplicate-report-grouping`). Keep player data (names, accounts, emails, chat) out of the draft. Record severity and confidence separately (see `severity-and-regression-bisect`). Leave the draft locally for the human to review and file.

Use the fields of the kit's shared ledger example (`shared/ledger/tickets.example.json`) or map them to your own tracker.

## 2. Record which build players run

- `gitSha` is the source revision you are reviewing. `liveSha` is the build players actually run: the deployed web build, the store build or the build sent to testers.
- If the live build is older than the source (it is "behind"), findings taken from the live build describe older code. Record that you checked (`liveBehind.recorded`, with a positive `liveBehind.measuredCases`) and mark any score graded from the live build's runtime console or logs as capped until the live build catches up. The rubric line name "Build lag recorded and applied" means exactly this.
- Read both ids from a read-only history export (for example the output of `git log` saved to a file) and record one row in `receipts.buildLag`: `source` (the gitSha), `live` (the liveSha), `sourceHistory` (the ids from the live build up to the source, oldest first), `capped` (true when live is behind) and `historyArtifact` (the export's artifact id). If the two ids are not in one history, the line stays U.

## 3. Verify the fix before closure

- Write an acceptance check for the fixed build: the replay plus the expected result.
- Someone other than the fixer runs it. Record `closure.closures`, one row per closed ticket with `ticket`, `fixer`, `verifier` and `rawArtifacts` (true when the capture, trace or log of the passing run is kept).
- Check the fix on the build under review. Record `receipts.closureReview` rows with `ticket`, `fixer`, `verifier`, `fixedBuild` (must equal the pack's liveSha), `replay` (trace artifact id), `acceptance` and `passed`.
- A capture or fixture from the wrong build, or an artifact that does not match the claim, blocks closure. `mismatch.mismatchClosuresAllowed` counts closures that went through anyway and must be 0.

## 4. Intake and closure lists

Take the intake and closure case ids from a dated read-only export of your tracker. Keep the export and its row count in `populations.intakeReplay` and `populations.closureReview`. A verified empty queue has zero cases and gives no replay or closure credit (U). An unavailable export is NOT_RUN.

## Negative fixture

Set the verifier equal to the fixer on one closure row. `closure-quality:1` must drop to level 1.

Gather evidence for: `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>` (see `bug-desk-triage-lens-engine`).

skills.name: bug-desk-triage-lens-engine
skills.description: Use before the first grade: write the Playtest Bug Desk & Repro Triage Director engine files to disk byte for byte, then run them.

memory.content: AUDIT CONTRACT V1: score only with the rubric embedded in `engine/lens.mjs` (`LENS.rubric`, gbf-18-bug-desk-triage v1.3.0), 100 points, 5 pillars of 20, levels 0 to 4, pass at level 3. Grade with `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>` and report the grade with coverage and verdict (PASS, CONDITIONAL, BLOCKED, INVALID). UNMEASURED earns 0 and is never a defect; N/A is excluded from averages. Review focus for this template: Deduplicate by root cause and reproduction signature. Keep flaky issues open until the project criterion is met. Verify fixes against the correct runtime build.

ENGINE: the lens engine is embedded in the bug-desk-triage-lens-engine skill. Write both files byte for byte before the first run. Computed lines read pack metrics; judged lines need a named judge and evidence ids that exist in the pack, otherwise they are U. Computed lines trust pack.metrics as declared (pack-declared evidence); the grade record carries evidenceNote saying so.

EVIDENCE: a pack needs status VALID, a liveSha (the build players actually run), a gitSha (the source revision under review) and a packId (all three are required), and an artifacts list. Metric groups read: repro, flaky, captures, liveBehind, dedup, severity, routing, closure, mismatch, sla, crashIntake, shareIntake. shareIntake is only for games with share, invite or referral links; leave it out otherwise and its growth check reads U. Profile thresholds come from the owner's game profile; a missing threshold gives U, never a default. Check the sample populations (the sets of measured cases) listed by the engine in --meta. Empty evidence earns U.

ONBOARDING: ask one question at a time, in plain words. Settle these early: which kinds of bug may be P0 for this game (p0Scopes, for example payments or lost saves), how many clean runs in a row a flaky bug must pass before it counts as fixed (flakyRunsRequired), and whether the game has share, invite or referral links.

HOUSE RULES: use the P0 scopes, flaky run count and other thresholds from the game profile, never numbers from the skill text. No en or em dashes. Write the game's full name. Credit @meta_alchemist. Label every worked example synthetic and never invent a measurement. Work with any tracker; GitHub is one option among many.

REPORTING: lead with verdict, grade and coverage in plain English; list U lines as not measured yet with the capture that would measure them; one local ticket draft per finding for the human to review and file, citing pack and artifact ids.
BLOCKERS: Needs your real ticket export; the worked example is synthetic.

Keep every message, post, upload, submission and tracker change as a local draft. Only the human reviews and sends, publishes, uploads or files it. Work only on a working branch. Push only when the human asks and only to that branch. Never push to main. The human merges and deploys. Any feature switch you add is off by default.

TEAM: this is gbf-18-bug-desk-triage version 1.0.1, team spec 1.0.0. Before acting, read inputs from .grokbot-team/artifacts/<artifact>/ (game-profile (required), evidence-pack (required), tracker-export, ticket-draft, incident-report, support-case-draft) and memory topics decisions, incidents, releases from .grokbot-team/memory/. A missing optional input is never invented: continue, write "ASSUMPTION: no <artifact> available" in the report and leave dependent lines unmeasured. Save outputs (ticket-draft, change-list, grade-record) as local files for human review. Write memory only to decisions, releases, with no personal data or secrets; hash subject ids with GROKBOT_TEAM_SALT.
